papers.title: Laser-Enabled Carbon Dot Coating for Powder Bed Fusion Metal Parts
papers.abstract: The development of environmentally friendly surface engineering techniques for 3D-printed metal parts is crucial for fluid-related applications. This study introduces two innovative, PFAS-free methods to achieve superhydrophilic surfaces on laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) fabricated AlSi10Mg and Ti6Al4V samples. The first method involves the direct application of gel-like carbon dots (G-CDs) coating inducing superhydrophilicity. The second method integrates nanosecond laser texturing to create microgrooves that facilitate capillary-driven liquid transport, followed by G-CDs coating, resulting in a stable superwicking surface. This laser-based method also offers precise control over fluid direction by adjusting the orientation of the microgrooves, allowing the surface to be designed with programmable wicking paths. Both methods maintain a water contact angle below 10° for over 30 days. Surface features, surface chemistry, wettability, wicking behavior are measured on AlSi10Mg and Ti6Al4V samples through Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Electron Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS), contact angle goniometer, and high-speed camera, respectively.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究Ti6Al4V和AlSi10Mg的表面涂层，未涉及力学或疲劳性能，因此与用户的Ti-6Al-4V力学/疲劳方向不相关。
llm.why_not_core: No mechanical or fatigue data for Ti-6Al-4V; focuses on surface wettability and coating, not mechanical performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 为3D打印金属部件开发环保的表面工程技术
summary_zh.method: 采用凝胶状碳点涂层结合激光织构化实现超亲水表面
summary_zh.result: 两种方法均使水接触角低于10°并持续30天以上，且激光织构可控制液体方向
summary_zh.validation: 通过SEM、EDS、接触角测量仪和高速相机表征表面性质

summary_en.motivation: Develop environmentally friendly surface engineering techniques for 3D-printed metal parts, specifically achieving superhydrophilic surfaces without PFAS.
summary_en.method: Two methods are introduced: direct gel-like carbon dot (G-CDs) coating, and nanosecond laser texturing to create microgrooves followed by G-CDs coating for stable superwicking surfaces.
summary_en.result: Both methods maintain water contact angle below 10° for over 30 days, with laser texturing enabling programmable wicking paths by adjusting microgroove orientation.
summary_en.validation: Surface features, chemistry, wettability, and wicking behavior are characterized using SEM, EDS, contact angle goniometry, and high-speed imaging.

papers.title: Laser Engineered Slippery Liquid Infused Porous Surfaces (SLIPS) on 3D Printed Metal Alloys
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) inherently produces metallic surfaces with high roughness and porosity, which limits their direct use in applications requiring low interfacial adhesion and controlled liquid mobility. In this work, a scalable strategy is presented for fabricating slippery liquid-infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) directly on as-printed L-PBF Ti6Al4V and AlSi10Mg alloys. Laser surface texturing using nanosecond and picosecond pulsed lasers was employed to restructure the irregular AM surface topography into well-defined microchannel networks that act as capillary reservoirs for lubricant retention. Following fluorosilane functionalization and silicone oil infusion, the resulting SLIPS exhibited static water contact angles exceeding 105° and sliding angles below 10°. Compared with untreated and laser-textured substrates, ice adhesion strength was reduced from approximately 370–460 kPa to ~65 kPa for Ti6Al4V and ~90 kPa for AlSi10Mg. The fabricated SLIPS maintained stable performance during repeated icing and deicing cycles and after mechanical abrasion, thermal exposure, and ultraviolet irradiation, indicating good durability and self-replenishing behavior. Overall, this work demonstrates a direct and versatile route for integrating SLIPS functionality with additively manufactured metal alloys, bridging L-PBF and laser surface engineering to enable durable anti-icing surfaces for aerospace, marine, and energy applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是Ti6Al4V合金的SLIPS表面防冰性能，而非力学或疲劳性能，因此与本方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on surface wettability and anti-icing properties via SLIPS, not on mechanical or fatigue characterization of Ti-6Al-4V; it does not provide tensile, fatigue, or other mechanical performance data.

summary_zh.motivation: 在L-PBF Ti6Al4V和AlSi10Mg合金上制造SLIPS以实现防冰。
summary_zh.method: 使用纳秒和皮秒脉冲激光进行表面纹理化，然后氟硅烷功能化和硅油注入。
summary_zh.result: 接触角>105°，滑动角<10°，冰粘附强度降至~65 kPa (Ti6Al4V) 和~90 kPa (AlSi10Mg)。
summary_zh.validation: 通过反复结冰-除冰循环、机械磨损、热暴露和紫外照射测试耐久性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a scalable method for fabricating slippery liquid-infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) on as-printed L-PBF Ti6Al4V and AlSi10Mg alloys for anti-icing applications.
summary_en.method: Used nanosecond and picosecond pulsed laser texturing to create microchannel networks, followed by fluorosilane functionalization and silicone oil infusion.
summary_en.result: The SLIPS exhibited static water contact angles >105°, sliding angles <10°, and reduced ice adhesion strength to ~65 kPa for Ti6Al4V and ~90 kPa for AlSi10Mg.
summary_en.validation: Durability was validated through repeated icing/deicing cycles, mechanical abrasion, thermal exposure, and UV irradiation.

papers.title: Investigation of surface integrity in ultrasonic vibration-assisted minimum quantity lubrication milling of Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled parts

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及传统铣削加工，而非增材制造后处理，与方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper studies conventional milling of Ti-6Al-4V, not a post-processing treatment for additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V, and thus falls outside the defined scope.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究超声振动辅助微量润滑铣削薄壁钛合金零件的表面完整性。
summary_zh.method: 采用超声振动辅助微量润滑铣削工艺加工Ti-6Al-4V薄壁件。
summary_zh.result: 分析了铣削参数对表面完整性的影响规律。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测量表面粗糙度和残余应力验证。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates surface integrity in ultrasonic vibration-assisted minimum quantity lubrication milling of Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled parts to improve machined surface quality.
summary_en.method: The authors employed ultrasonic vibration-assisted minimum quantity lubrication (UVAMQL) milling on Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled workpieces and characterized surface roughness, residual stress, and microhardness.
summary_en.result: It was found that UVAMQL milling reduces surface roughness and introduces compressive residual stress compared to conventional milling.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of surface roughness and residual stress validated the improvements.
